---
title: "CP Initialization and Convergence"
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{CP Initialization and Convergence}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::knitr}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7.2,
  fig.height = 4.6,
  fig.align = "center",
  dpi = 120
)

palette <- c(
  "CP-ALS" = "#4D4D4D",
  "RGD" = "#D55E00",
  "RGN" = "#0072B2",
  "CPCA" = "#0072B2",
  "HOSVD" = "#D55E00"
)
method_lty <- c("CP-ALS" = 3, "RGD" = 2, "RGN" = 1)
method_pch <- c("CP-ALS" = 15, "RGD" = 17, "RGN" = 16)

locate_extdata <- function() {
  installed <- system.file(
    "extdata", "rebuttal_init", package = "SegreCP"
  )
  candidates <- c(
    file.path("inst", "extdata", "rebuttal_init"),
    file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", "rebuttal_init"),
    installed
  )
  candidates <- candidates[nzchar(candidates)]
  found <- candidates[dir.exists(candidates)]
  if (!length(found)) {
    stop("Cannot locate the frozen rebuttal initializer-sensitivity data.")
  }
  normalizePath(found[[1L]], mustWork = TRUE)
}

read_artifact <- function(section, file) {
  utils::read.csv(
    file.path(extdata_root, section, file),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}

extdata_root <- locate_extdata()

decomp_results <- read_artifact("decomp_ref", "trajectory_raw.csv")
decomp_initialization <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_ref", "initialization_summary.csv"
)
decomp_checks <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_ref", "validation_checks.csv"
)

objective_results <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_objective", "trajectory_raw.csv"
)
objective_checks <- read_artifact(
  "decomp_objective", "validation_checks.csv"
)

regression_init <- read_artifact(
  "reg_ref", "initialization_summary.csv"
)
regression_checks <- read_artifact(
  "reg_ref", "validation_checks.csv"
)

decomp_pass_col <- if ("passed" %in% names(decomp_checks)) {
  "passed"
} else {
  "pass"
}
objective_pass_col <- if ("passed" %in% names(objective_checks)) {
  "passed"
} else {
  "pass"
}
regression_pass_col <- if ("passed" %in% names(regression_checks)) {
  "passed"
} else {
  "pass"
}

stopifnot(
  all(decomp_checks[[decomp_pass_col]]),
  all(objective_checks[[objective_pass_col]]),
  all(regression_checks[[regression_pass_col]]),
  nrow(decomp_results) == 20L * 2L * 3L * 11L,
  nrow(objective_results) == 20L * 2L * 3L * 11L,
  identical(sort(unique(decomp_results$iteration)), 0:10),
  identical(sort(unique(objective_results$iteration)), 0:10),
  all(c("CPCA", "HOSVD") %in% decomp_results$initialization),
  all(c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN") %in% decomp_results$method)
)

mean_trajectory <- function(x) {
  aggregate(
    relative_frobenius_error ~ initialization + method + iteration,
    x,
    mean
  )
}

decomp_mean <- mean_trajectory(decomp_results)

stopifnot(
  "objective" %in% names(objective_results),
  all(is.finite(objective_results$objective))
)
objective_raw <- objective_results[order(
  objective_results$replication,
  objective_results$initialization,
  objective_results$method,
  objective_results$iteration
), ]
objective_key <- interaction(
  objective_raw$replication,
  objective_raw$initialization,
  objective_raw$method,
  drop = TRUE
)
objective_raw$objective_ratio <- objective_raw$objective /
  ave(objective_raw$objective, objective_key, FUN = function(z) z[[1L]])
objective_mean <- aggregate(
  objective_ratio ~ initialization + method + iteration,
  objective_raw,
  mean
)

objective_path_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(objective_raw, objective_key),
  function(z) {
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    data.frame(
      initialization = z$initialization[[1L]],
      method = z$method[[1L]],
      max_objective_increase = max(c(0, diff(z$objective)))
    )
  }
))

oracle_source <- objective_results
oracle_key <- interaction(
  oracle_source$replication,
  oracle_source$initialization,
  oracle_source$method,
  drop = TRUE
)
oracle_path_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(oracle_source, oracle_key),
  function(z) {
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    increases <- diff(z$relative_frobenius_error)
    data.frame(
      initialization = z$initialization[[1L]],
      method = z$method[[1L]],
      path_increases = any(increases > 1e-12),
      max_oracle_increase = max(c(0, increases))
    )
  }
))

oracle_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(
    oracle_path_stats,
    interaction(
      oracle_path_stats$initialization,
      oracle_path_stats$method,
      drop = TRUE
    )
  ),
  function(z) {
    data.frame(
      Initialization = z$initialization[[1L]],
      Method = z$method[[1L]],
      Paths = nrow(z),
      `Paths with an oracle-error increase` = sum(z$path_increases),
      `Largest increase` = max(z$max_oracle_increase),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
))
rownames(oracle_summary) <- NULL
```

This vignette plots the recorded CPCA-versus-HOSVD experiment. Each mean uses
20 paired replications. To generate new data and refit RGD/RGN under the same
design, use the [simulation scripts](https://github.com/kxu-stat/SegreCP/blob/main/reproducibility/simulations/README.md).

The decomposition experiment uses dimensions `60 x 30 x 30`, CP rank 3,
condition number 30, coherence 0.5, noise standard deviation 1, and 10 complete
outer sweeps. The regression rows use a `10 x 10` tensor response and a
`10 x 10 x 10` tensor predictor. Comparisons are paired within a row; values
should not be compared across the decomposition and regression tasks.

## Initialization sensitivity

The first diagnostic asks whether CPCA and HOSVD enter the refinement stage at
comparable errors. Both quantities are relative Frobenius errors: tensor error
for decomposition and coefficient error for regression. Error bars are the
frozen 95% bootstrap intervals.

```{r initialization-sensitivity, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="Initial relative Frobenius error under CPCA and HOSVD. Intervals are frozen 95% bootstrap intervals over 20 paired replications; comparisons are within rows."}
decomp_initial_plot <- data.frame(
  setting = "Decomposition (0.5, 1)",
  initialization = decomp_initialization$initialization,
  mean = decomp_initialization$initial_error_mean,
  lower = decomp_initialization$ci_lower,
  upper = decomp_initialization$ci_upper,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

regression_initial_plot <- data.frame(
  setting = sprintf(
    "Regression (%g, %g)",
    regression_init$coherence,
    regression_init$noise_sd
  ),
  initialization = regression_init$initialization,
  mean = regression_init$initial_error_mean,
  lower = regression_init$initial_error_lower,
  upper = regression_init$initial_error_upper,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

initial_plot <- rbind(decomp_initial_plot, regression_initial_plot)
setting_order <- c(
  "Decomposition (0.5, 1)",
  "Regression (0, 0.5)",
  "Regression (0, 1)",
  "Regression (0.5, 0.5)",
  "Regression (0.5, 1)"
)
initial_plot$y <- match(initial_plot$setting, rev(setting_order))

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(4.2, 8.2, 2.6, 0.8), las = 1)
plot(
  range(initial_plot$lower, initial_plot$upper),
  range(initial_plot$y) + c(-0.45, 0.45),
  type = "n",
  axes = FALSE,
  xlab = "Initial relative Frobenius error",
  ylab = "",
  main = "CPCA and HOSVD initialization error"
)
axis(1, col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
axis(
  2,
  at = seq_along(setting_order),
  labels = rev(setting_order),
  tick = FALSE,
  cex.axis = 0.86
)
abline(h = seq_along(setting_order), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 1)
for (initializer in c("CPCA", "HOSVD")) {
  z <- initial_plot[initial_plot$initialization == initializer, ]
  offset <- if (initializer == "CPCA") 0.09 else -0.09
  segments(
    z$lower, z$y + offset, z$upper, z$y + offset,
    col = palette[[initializer]], lwd = 2
  )
  points(
    z$mean, z$y + offset,
    col = palette[[initializer]],
    pch = if (initializer == "CPCA") 16 else 17,
    cex = 1.05
  )
}
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c("CPCA", "HOSVD"),
  col = palette[c("CPCA", "HOSVD")],
  pch = c(16, 17),
  bty = "n",
  horiz = TRUE,
  inset = c(0, -0.01)
)
box(bty = "l", col = "#666666")
par(old_par)
```

CPCA has the lower mean initial error in every displayed setting. This is an
initialization comparison, not evidence that one optimizer must have the best
terminal error.

## Full decomposition trajectories

The next figure shows mean relative tensor error through ten outer sweeps,
separately for CPCA and HOSVD initialization.

```{r decomposition-trajectories, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.6, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Mean relative tensor error over 10 sweeps, averaged over 20 paired replications."}
trajectory_ylim <- range(decomp_mean$relative_frobenius_error)
trajectory_ylim <- trajectory_ylim + c(-0.02, 0.02) * diff(trajectory_ylim)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.7, 3.0, 0.8),
  oma = c(0, 0, 1.0, 0), las = 1
)
for (initializer in c("CPCA", "HOSVD")) {
  plot(
    0:10,
    rep(NA_real_, 11),
    type = "n",
    ylim = trajectory_ylim,
    xlab = "Completed outer sweeps",
    ylab = "Mean relative tensor error",
    main = paste(initializer, "initialization"),
    axes = FALSE
  )
  axis(1, at = seq(0, 10, by = 2), col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  axis(2, col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  abline(h = pretty(trajectory_ylim), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 1)
  box(bty = "l", col = "#666666")

  for (method in c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")) {
    z <- decomp_mean[
      decomp_mean$initialization == initializer &
        decomp_mean$method == method,
    ]
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]

    lines(
      z$iteration,
      z$relative_frobenius_error,
      col = palette[[method]],
      lty = method_lty[[method]],
      lwd = 2.1
    )
    points(
      z$iteration,
      z$relative_frobenius_error,
      col = palette[[method]],
      pch = method_pch[[method]],
      cex = 0.68
    )
  }

  if (initializer == "CPCA") {
    legend(
      "topright",
      legend = c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN"),
      col = palette[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      pch = method_pch[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lty = method_lty[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lwd = 1.8,
      bty = "n",
      cex = 0.80
    )
  }
}
mtext("Decomposition error by initialization", outer = TRUE)
par(old_par)
```

## Observed-objective convergence

Recorded CP-ALS, RGD, and RGN fits provide the observed least-squares
objective at each completed sweep. The figure normalizes each replication by
its initial objective and then averages the ratios.

```{r objective-convergence, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=4.1, fig.cap="Mean observed-objective ratio over 20 recorded runs; the vertical axis shows the observed range."}
objective_ylim <- range(objective_mean$objective_ratio)
objective_ylim <- c(
  floor(100 * objective_ylim[[1L]]) / 100,
  min(1.005, objective_ylim[[2L]] + 0.005)
)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.8, 3.0, 0.8),
  oma = c(0, 0, 1.0, 0), las = 1
)
for (initializer in c("CPCA", "HOSVD")) {
  plot(
    0:10,
    rep(NA_real_, 11),
    type = "n",
    ylim = objective_ylim,
    xlab = "Completed outer sweeps",
    ylab = "Mean objective / initial objective",
    main = paste(initializer, "initialization"),
    axes = FALSE
  )
  axis(1, at = seq(0, 10, by = 2), col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  axis(2, col = "#666666", col.axis = "#333333")
  abline(h = pretty(objective_ylim), col = "#ECECEC", lwd = 1)
  box(bty = "l", col = "#666666")

  for (method in c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")) {
    z <- objective_mean[
      objective_mean$initialization == initializer &
        objective_mean$method == method,
    ]
    z <- z[order(z$iteration), ]
    lines(
      z$iteration,
      z$objective_ratio,
      col = palette[[method]],
      lty = method_lty[[method]],
      lwd = 2
    )
    points(
      z$iteration,
      z$objective_ratio,
      col = palette[[method]],
      pch = method_pch[[method]],
      cex = 0.72
    )
  }
  if (initializer == "CPCA") {
    legend(
      "topright",
      legend = c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN"),
      col = palette[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lty = method_lty[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      pch = method_pch[c("CP-ALS", "RGD", "RGN")],
      lwd = 2,
      bty = "n",
      cex = 0.82
    )
  }
}
mtext("Observed objective convergence (focused vertical scale)", outer = TRUE)
par(old_par)
```

```{r objective-check, echo=FALSE}
objective_check <- data.frame(
  Recorded.paths = nrow(objective_path_stats),
  Paths.with.an.increase = sum(
    objective_path_stats$max_objective_increase > 1e-10
  ),
  Largest.increase = max(objective_path_stats$max_objective_increase),
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(objective_check) <- c(
  "Recorded paths", "Paths with an increase", "Largest increase"
)
knitr::kable(objective_check, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
```

## Oracle error and the noise floor

The relative error to the simulated truth is scientifically useful, but it is
not the objective minimized by the algorithms. Consequently, an individual
oracle-error path may rise slightly after reaching the statistical noise floor
even while the observed objective continues to decrease.

```{r oracle-floor-summary, echo=FALSE}
oracle_display <- oracle_summary
oracle_display[["Largest increase"]] <- format(
  oracle_display[["Largest increase"]],
  scientific = TRUE,
  digits = 3
)
knitr::kable(oracle_display, row.names = FALSE)
```

This distinction is why the full trajectories are reported as empirical
convergence diagnostics rather than as evidence of global convergence or
per-replication monotonicity of the unknown-truth error.
